input: Brew a first batch of homemade kombucha

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Whether this is a straightforward first fermentation (F1) only, or if the user also wants to do a second fermentation (F2) for carbonation and flavouring, significantly changes the steps, equipment, and timeline involved.
Knowing if the user already has a SCOBY and starter liquid, or needs to acquire or grow one first, determines whether the plan starts at sourcing or at brewing.
Budget affects which equipment the user can buy (e.g., a purpose-built brewing kit vs. improvising with household items) and which tea or sugar options are realistic.
The home environment — available counter space, ambient temperature, and kitchen setup — directly affects fermentation time and where the vessel can safely sit undisturbed.
Preferred flavour profile (plain, fruity, gingery, etc.) and tea base (black, green, white) shapes the recipe chosen for the very first batch.

Understanding what success looks like — a drinkable result, a specific level of tartness, or simply completing the process without mistakes — sets the right level of detail and safety checks in the plan.
The batch size (e.g., 1 litre vs. 4 litres) determines vessel size, ingredient quantities, and how much the user needs to invest upfront for a first attempt.

gold.taskTitle: Brew a first batch of homemade kombucha
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to successfully produce their first homemade kombucha brew from scratch.

questions.title: Will you only do first fermentation, or also second fermentation for fizz?
questions.description: Determines whether the plan covers F1 only (plain kombucha) or extends to F2 (bottling with fruit/juice for carbonation).

questions.title: Do you already have a SCOBY and starter liquid?
questions.description: Establishes whether the plan needs a sourcing or SCOBY-growing phase before any brewing can begin.

questions.title: What is your budget for equipment and ingredients?
questions.description: Shapes whether to recommend a dedicated brewing kit, repurposed glass jars, and which tea and sugar options are practical.

questions.title: How warm is the space where the brew will sit?
questions.description: Ambient temperature is the biggest environmental variable — it directly controls fermentation speed and determines how to judge readiness.

questions.title: What flavour profile are you hoping the kombucha has?
questions.description: Guides the choice of tea base and any fruit or spice additions, shaping the core recipe from day one.

questions.title: What will make this first batch feel like a success to you?
questions.description: Clarifies the target outcome — whether it is simply finishing the process, achieving a specific tartness, or producing a certain volume of drinkable kombucha.

questions.title: How large a batch do you want to brew this first time?
questions.description: Determines vessel size, ingredient quantities, and overall investment level for the initial attempt.
